notes: Read all three target units, full Social Security context, all eleven candidates and the review. Resolved the commission, bills, proposals and legislation to Social Security reform, while keeping the commission models and congressional bills distinct. Restored U.S. scope to the homeownership assertions and retained the asserted four-year causal link from improved capital and credit access to record homeownership.

claims.claim_text: President Bush formed a bipartisan commission that recommended three Social Security reform models.
Many congressional Republicans sponsored six Social Security reform bills, which the platform characterizes as leadership.
Nonpartisan analysis found that each of the three commission models and six congressional Social Security proposals would strengthen Social Security.
Each of the three commission models and six congressional Social Security proposals would let workers supplement Social Security with personally owned retirement accounts.
Support for President Bush and congressional Republicans' efforts to enact Social Security reform legislation during the next presidential term.
Over the preceding four years, U.S. entrepreneurs' access to capital and consumers' access to credit improved immensely, reportedly producing record U.S. homeownership.
For the first time, more than half of U.S. minority-group members owned their homes.
